assets.title: First image of M87*
assets.classification: Observation reconstructed from real radio telescope measurements
assets.alt: The Event Horizon Telescope image of M87 star, showing a bright orange ring surrounding a dark central shadow.
assets.caption: M87* at 1.3 millimeters. Orange is a display choice applied to radio data.

assets.title: First image of Sagittarius A*
assets.classification: Observation reconstructed from real radio telescope measurements and presented as an averaged image
assets.alt: The Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A star, showing a bright orange ring surrounding a dark central shadow.
assets.caption: Sagittarius A* is an average assembled from many reconstructions compatible with the 2017 observations.

assets.title: Sagittarius A* reconstruction comparison
assets.alt: A comparison of Sagittarius A star reconstruction groups and the published average.
assets.caption: Representative reconstruction groups shown beside the published average.

assets.title: M87* and Sagittarius A* scale comparison
assets.alt: A comparison graphic showing the physical scales associated with M87 star and Sagittarius A star.
assets.caption: A common-scale comparison supplied by the EHT Collaboration.

assets.title: Messier 87 galaxy
assets.alt: An optical observation of the giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87.
assets.caption: Messier 87 observed with FORS2 on ESO’s Very Large Telescope.

assets.title: ALMA antennas at Chajnantor

assets.caption: Human observers and instruments beneath the night sky.

assets.title: Event Horizon Telescope observatory map

assets.caption: Observatories participating in the EHT network and later additions.

assets.title: Stars orbiting the Milky Way’s central black hole
assets.alt: A time-lapse of stars moving around the center of the Milky Way.
assets.caption: Nearly twenty years of observations compressed into about twenty seconds.
assets.transcript: Stars move rapidly around an apparently empty central point. A diagram overlay may trace one selected orbit.

assets.title: Labeled accretion-disk visualization

assets.alt: A labeled scientific visualization showing a black-hole shadow, photon ring, and lensed images of an accretion disk.
assets.caption: A calculated visualization identifying the visible surroundings of a black hole.

assets.title: Black-hole optics diagram
assets.credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Jeremy Schnittman
assets.license: NASA media usage guidelines; asset-level third-party notice must be checked
assets.alt: A diagram showing direct and bent light paths from an accretion disk around a black hole.
assets.caption: Light from different parts of the disk reaches the observer along curved paths.

assets.title: Edge-on accretion-disk animation
assets.classification: Scientific visualization calculated from physical models
assets.credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Jeremy Schnittman
assets.license: NASA media usage guidelines; asset-level third-party notice must be checked
assets.alt: A calculated edge-on visualization of an accretion disk warped by black-hole gravity.
assets.caption: Calculated visualization, not telescope footage.
assets.transcript: The far side and underside of the disk appear above and below the black hole because gravity bends their light.

assets.title: Rotating accretion-disk visualization
assets.classification: Scientific visualization calculated from physical models
assets.credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Jeremy Schnittman
assets.license: NASA media usage guidelines; asset-level third-party notice must be checked
assets.alt: A calculated visualization showing how an accretion disk’s apparent shape changes with viewing angle.
assets.caption: Calculated viewing-angle visualization, not a photograph.
assets.transcript: The viewpoint changes around the modeled black hole, revealing changing lensed images of the disk.
